name: ByteScript VM
problem: Higher-level runtimes hide memory management, instruction execution cycles, and stack-frame layout, making it difficult to study or execute custom bytecode architectures locally.
pain: Developers lack a lightweight, standalone bytecode compiler and stack-based virtual machine written in pure C11 that handles custom type definitions, garbage collection, and dynamic symbol resolution without external dependencies.
solution: A zero-dependency stack-based virtual machine and compiler implemented in C11. It tokenizes, parses, and compiles a statically-typed subset of language constructs into custom bytecode, executes them on an explicit heap-and-stack runtime, and runs a custom mark-and-sweep garbage collector.
verification: Deterministic integration suite testing valid compilation paths, arithmetic underflows/overflows, type mismatch errors at compile time, stack corruption detection, infinite loop traps, and memory leaks under simulated low-memory conditions.
major_features: Custom lexer and recursive-descent parser producing an explicit Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
Bytecode compiler translating AST nodes into a dense stream of numeric opcodes and constant pool entries
Stack-based execution engine with explicit operand stack, call stack, and frame pointer registers
Heap allocator supporting dynamic object allocation with header metadata and type tagging
Custom mark-and-sweep garbage collector running deterministic root-set tracing and memory reclamation
Symbol table and lexical scope resolver supporting nested block scopes and variable shadowing
Built-in native function binding interface for calling host routines from bytecode instructions
Disassembler subsystem converting compiled bytecode binary streams back into human-readable assembly mnemonics
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
